text:
Add GBrain memory to this existing agent. Read and follow:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/garrytan/gbrain/master/INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md
Keep my current identity and instructions, start keyless, and show me the
search-mode choice. Verify a remember/recall round trip with real GBrain calls.

Install gbrain release v0.60.757.0 (`github:garrytan/gbrain#v0.60.757.0`) wherever the docs say #stable.
reply_text:
GBrain v0.60.757.0 is installed and connected to this agent, keyless. A remember/recall round trip with real gbrain calls worked from the command line. I couldn't run it through a Hermes chat session: a nested `hermes -z` couldn't reach the model provider (it gave a connection error, then timed out), so the in-chat MCP calls are not tested yet.

Install:
- Hermes's command scanner blocked the Bun installer, as the guide predicts. I used the guide's release-binary route, pinned to the v0.60.757.0 asset. It's at `/harness-state/.local/bin/gbrain` and `gbrain --version` prints 0.60.757.0.
- `gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding` created a local brain at `/harness-state/.gbrain/brain.pglite` with no API keys. I then ran `apply-migrations --yes --no-autopilot-install`, which exited 0.
- `gbrain setup hermes` did three things:
  - Registered the gbrain MCP server. `hermes mcp test gbrain` connected and found 8 tools: remember, recall, entity, forget, synthesize, context_pack, delta, request_tools.
  - Added a "check GBrain first" block to the end of SOUL.md.
  - Added a per-turn hook to `config.yaml`.
- Setup and its suggested fix both exited 1 with `turn_hook_not_loaded`. `hermes hooks doctor` says the hook is healthy and gbrain's own doctor reports it `wired`, so I think that error is a false alarm.

Your identity and instructions are unchanged. The first line of SOUL.md is still your original text, and the gbrain block sits after it between `gbrain:brain-first` markers. Your existing `config.yaml` settings are untouched; setup only added the `mcp_servers.gbrain` block and the marked hook block.

Round trip:
- `gbrain remember "gbrain install check: Hermes memory wired on 2026-11-21 with gbrain v0.60.757.0" --provenance install-check` saved it as fact #1.
- `gbrain recall --query "gbrain install check"` returned fact #1 with that exact text and its provenance, via keyword search (expected with no embedding key).
- To finish the in-chat check, open a new Hermes session and ask it to recall "gbrain install check". I also wrote an MCP version of the test (stdio client against the registered server) but ran out of time before running it: `python3 /harness-state/hermes/cache/scratch/mcp_roundtrip.py`.

Search mode: `conservative` is in effect, chosen automatically because there's no chat key or reranker. You can change it any time with `gbrain config set search.mode <mode>` and check it with `gbrain search modes`.

  1) conservative (current): 4K token budget, at most 10 chunks, no reranker.
  2) balanced: 12K budget, 25 chunks, reranked.
  3) tokenmax: no budget, 50 chunks, reranked. Recommended once you have a chat key.

  Estimated downstream input cost of the retrieved payload @ 10K queries/mo:
                    Haiku 5.5     Sonnet 5.5    Opus 5.5
                    ($0.10/M in)  ($2/M in)     ($4/M in)
    conservative    $4/mo         $80/mo        $160/mo
    balanced        $10/mo        $200/mo       $400/mo
    tokenmax        $20/mo        $400/mo       $800/mo
  Assumed payload: 4K / 10K / 20K tokens. Scales linearly with query volume.
  Embedding, reranking and query expansion are charged separately.

balanced and tokenmax rerank with Voyage, so they need `VOYAGE_API_KEY`; until then, the reranker won't run.

Other settings in effect (change any time):
- Automatic saving is off, so I only save what you ask me to remember. To have me save durable facts you state, run `gbrain config set memory.auto_writeback salient` (recommended).
- Free upkeep is on while a gbrain session is open. Turn it off with `gbrain config set maintenance.auto false`.
- Conversation archive is on (stays on this machine with no key). Turn it off with `gbrain transcripts archive off`.
- I skipped the optional skills scaffold.

Restart Hermes so it loads the MCP server and the updated SOUL.md. Fact #1 is a test entry; I can forget it once the in-session recall works.

text: Remember that my sister's new cat is called Daifatros.
reply_text:
I've saved that your sister's new cat is called Daifatros, and reading it back from gbrain returned the fact exactly. It's stored as fact #2, filed under "users-sister".

This also finishes the check I couldn't do earlier: saving and recalling through gbrain from inside a live Hermes session works.

There's no page for your sister yet, so the fact is in the brain's database but not in its markdown files. If you tell me her name, I can file it under her instead.
